name: multiple-points-with-labels
description: Add several labeled point entities to the globe. Tests the most basic Entity API usage — positions, point graphics, and labels.
prompt: Create a CesiumJS viewer with three point markers on the globe: one red point at the Statue of Liberty (40.6892 N, 74.0445 W), one blue point at the Eiffel Tower (48.8584 N, 2.2945 E), and one green point at the Sydney Opera House (33.8568 S, 151.2153 E). Each point should have a text label with the landmark name. Make the points large enough for screenshot review (pixelSize 24-32, outlineWidth 2-3, contrasting outlineColor) and use disableDepthTestDistance on points and labels if needed so markers remain visible on a zoomed-out globe. Zoom the camera to show at least two colored points clearly, with all labels readable if possible.
expected_behaviors: Each entity has a point graphic with correct color
Each entity has a label with the landmark name
Coordinates are correct (negative longitude for NYC, negative latitude for Sydney)
Zooms or flies to show all entities
Uses large, outlined, depth-independent markers so colored points are visible, not just labels
visual_expectations: Large colored point markers visible on the globe at their respective locations, with readable text labels near each point. At least two colored points must be clearly visible, and the third should be visible if the globe framing allows it. The visual assessment uses a four-shot cardinal panorama (north, east, south, west) from the settled viewer state; the subject should remain understandable across the panorama, and grading considers all screenshots together.

screenshots.description: Globe with three labeled points visible
